title: Krishna and the handful of rice
hookLine: Krishna knows why his poor friend has come and spares him the asking; Patanjali says a yogi can know another's mood, but not its reason
carry: a mood can be known; its reason is theirs
last: SIDDHI: SEE CHANGE FULLY, AND TIME OPENS.

lines: A POOR FRIEND, A RAG OF RICE.
HE CAN'T BRING HIMSELF TO ASK.
cards: A poor brahmin and his wife have almost nothing to eat. She reminds him: your old school friend is Krishna, a king now, in Dvaraka. Go and see him.
He's too proud to beg, but he goes, carrying the only gift they could find: a few handfuls of flattened rice, begged from neighbors and tied in a rag.
The Bhagavata Purana calls him only a poor friend; many families call him Sudama. At the palace, Krishna jumps up from his queen's couch, runs to him, hugs him, and washes his feet.

teach.b: They sit and talk about their school days, and the friend can't bring himself to ask for anything, or even hand over his little bundle. He's ashamed of it.
The text says Krishna, who sees into every heart, knew exactly why he had come. So he didn't make him ask.
He pulled out the bundle himself, ate a handful of the rice with delight, and sent his friend home without a word about money. At home, the friend's hut has become a palace.
In the story Krishna is God, who knows each heart from the inside. Patanjali describes something smaller, a power of a human yogi, and he draws a careful line around it.

teach.h: PRATYAYA: WHAT'S IN A MIND NOW.
teach.b: Sutra 3.19: by samyama on the idea in another's mind, pratyaya, knowledge of that mind. Its color: troubled, calm, glad, afraid. Then 3.20, straight away: but not its object.

teach.h: KNOW THE MIND, NOT ITS OBJECT.
teach.b: You can know that a mind is anxious, not what it's anxious about. The power reaches the state, not the whole story. Notice the order of the eight limbs, too.
They don't begin with powers. They begin with non-harm. And Krishna, who did know everything, used it to protect his friend's dignity.
So the teaching runs both ways: even at its height, knowing another mind has a limit, and what you do with what you sense matters more than the sensing.

teach.h: A MOOD CAN BE KNOWN; ITS REASON IS THEIRS.
teach.b: The week, from the top: the wind that stopped, Shiva's closed eyes, the bird's head, Ekalavya's clay teacher, the king's palanquin, Vyasa's warning, and a handful of rice.

how: The story of Krishna and his poor friend is told to Hindu children everywhere, and some temples, like Guruvayur in Kerala, keep a day when devotees offer Krishna flattened rice in his memory; teachers of the Yoga Sutras point to 3.20's limit and to the yamas as the frame in which any such power is held.

o: a promise you make at the start of each day
a guess about what someone will do next
the idea or mood in a mind right now

games.q: the power and its limit — tap the pairs.
p: the idea in a mind right now
but not what it's fixed on
knew, and spared his friend asking

s: 3.19 says the yogi reads every detail of another's thoughts
3.20 says not its object: the state of the mind, not what it's about.
in the story, Krishna made his friend ask for help out loud
he knew why his friend had come, and spared him the asking.
the limit is stated in the very next sutra

games.q: you sense a friend's mind is angry. by sutra 3.20, what can you know?
o: that the mind is angry, but not at what.
exactly who they're angry at, and why.
games.why: 3.20: but not its object, since that wasn't the object of the samyama. the power reaches the color of the mind, not its whole story.

practice: Ask what color your own mind is right now, restless, tired, glad, worried, and name it in one word without chasing the reasons. Breathe with it.
Then, if you like, bring to mind someone you love and wish their mind well, whatever color it is today.

wordCard.voice: Pratyaya, the mood or idea running through someone's awareness. By samyama on another's state of mind, that mind is known, though not what it's fixed on.

orig.note: Sanskrit para-citta-jñāna: knowledge (jñāna) of another's (para) mind (citta), 3.19.

carryVoice: Your line: a mood can be known; its reason is theirs. So reach out, and ask kindly. A week of the inner limbs, done.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.80–10.81 (Krishna and his poor brahmin friend; the flattened rice)
